title: paged-kv-write-ahead-checkpoint-and-residency-hysteresis-observability
creator: Asha Menon
description: Design and implement a write-ahead checkpoint (WAL) for the paged/blocked KV cache to enable safe async spill-to-host and deterministic recovery, together with a residency hysteresis controller and observability surfaces that make GPU memory paging behavior visible to SREs and product. This ticket covers: WAL format decisions, durable checkpointing triggers, residency watermarks with hysteresis to avoid oscillation, host spill/restore orchestration, and new metrics/logs/dashboards for debugging page faults and tail latency. Goal: reduce OOM incidents during bursty batched workloads and make paging behavior debuggable for customers using Dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: WAL write path integrated into paged-kv hot path with <5% p99 token latency regression on benchmark X
On-disk checkpoint format documented and backward-compatible with existing recovery util
Residency hysteresis controller implemented with configurable high/low watermarks (defaults: 82% high, 68% low) to avoid rapid evict/restore oscillation
Host spill/restore flow executes asynchronously and resiliently: partial restores handled without corrupting live KV state
New observability: per-GPU residency histogram, page-fault/sec, avg/95/99 restore latency, WAL throughput, and spill rate; dashboards created in Grafana
E2E tests that simulate sudden 2x batch surge and validate no unrecoverable OOM and bounded tail latency increase
implementation_notes: WAL format: append-only segmented files with index: <segment-id>|<start-slot>|<slot-count>|crc32; segments rotate when >=64MB or after N ops
Checkpoint triggers: (1) residency high watermark breached; (2) periodic low-latency background checkpoint every 30s; (3) graceful shutdown/worker recycle
Spill policy: prefer coalesced slot ranges (block-aligned) to minimize host IOPS and CPU decompress overhead; use per-GPU async IO thread pool
Residency controller: implement hysteresis to dampen churn. Default hysteresis gap 14 percentage points. Expose tunables per-tenant on Dedicated.

Concurrency: WAL writes must be non-blocking for inference threads — use bounded MPSC ring buffer + background flusher. Background flusher must implement backpressure when host write latency > 200ms to avoid unbounded memory growth.
Restore: on-demand lazy restore for a slot first accessed after spill; optimistic read path tries to reconstruct KV from partial in-memory metadata before blocking on host IO.

Fallbacks: when WAL throughput/backpressure indicates host is overloaded, trigger graceful model fallback (quantized variant) or route requests to lower-tier capacity per smart-routing policy. Integrate with runtime fallbacks in routing layer.
Compatibility: keep on-disk segments checksummed; version header allows rolling upgrades between runtime-1.21 and 1.22. Include migration doc link in PR.

Observability: emit structured events for: WAL-segment-closed, spill-start/complete, restore-start/complete, residency-high-triggered, residency-low-clear. Counters + histograms: wal_bytes_written_total, wal_segment_count, spill_ops_total, restore_latency_seconds_bucket, residency_percentiles
Perf target: WAL flusher should sustain >600MB/s aggregate per host under steady-state spill scenarios without increasing p95 latency by >8ms on synthetic streaming benchmark
risks: Host I/O bottlenecks can turn a safe spill into a latency storm — mitigate by throttling and user-visible fallback policies
Incorrect hysteresis tuning could leave GPU underutilized or cause delayed paging leading to sudden large spills
WAL corruption risk if segment rotation and flush ordering aren't carefully atomic; must add CRC + atomic rename
Complexity in multi-GPU setups when same logical KV ranges are sharded across GPUs; need to coordinate spill decisions to avoid cascading restores
test_plan: Unit tests for WAL append/rotate/verify with injected IO failures
Integration test: simulated 3-GPU box with synthetic bursts that trigger residency high watermark; assert spill completed and restores succeed under concurrent inference
Chaos test: random host write latencies and mid-spill worker kills; validate deterministic recovery and no data corruption
Performance benchmark: end-to-end p50/p95/p99 token latency for streaming prompt workloads with and without WAL enabled; measure CPU and host IO utilization
Regression: add to nightly E2E where we replay production trace with known hotset to verify hysteresis reduces oscillation

comments: 2025-02-13 | Asha Menon: Initial draft added. Key open questions: WAL segment sizing tradeoffs and whether to compress segments with lz4 by default.
2025-02-14 | Diego Ramos: Reviewed. Favor 64MB segment default; lz4 compression optional via runtime flag. Need benchmarks for CPU overhead. Assigned to Diego for prototype implementation.
2025-02-18 | Priya Shah (SRE): Observability hooks look good. Request that we add a high-cardinality tag for customer_id on spill events for Dedicated so SRE can correlate with tenant load.

2025-02-21 | Diego Ramos: Prototype WAL flusher implemented (branch: feat/wal-flusher). Found edge case where concurrent segment rotation + worker crash left temporary file; fixed with atomic rename and tmp suffix.
2025-02-25 | QA: Started integration runs. Observed increased host write latency in one testbed due to noisy neighbor; added backpressure cap to flusher (max_inflight_segments=4).
2025-03-01 | Diego Ramos: Residency hysteresis controller merged to canary. Default high/low watermarks set to 82%/68%. Still tuning hysteresis gap after canary telemetry.
